messages:
alex_chen: Heads-up — we're seeing a memory surge / OOMs on prod inference cluster `inference-1` starting ~12:10 UTC right after the runtime deploy. Errors are `cudamalloc` failures. stack traces reference the new fused kernel path. Anyone on call?

deploy-bot: automated-deploy: commit a7f9c2 enabled kernel 'fused-gemm-v2' and bumped default workspace to 512MB at 12:06 UTC. Canary passed.

maria_gomez: I pulled a short profile (link: https://internal.gists/redwood/prof/184750) — samples show GPU mem high growth during decode for long-context requests. median workspace per-request jumped ~1.8x vs previous kernel.

sam_patel: Looks like fused-gemm-v2 triggers a different workspace allocation pattern + larger temporary buffers for attention causal. KV cache footprint also creeps because we don't reuse some temporary buffers between batches. snippet from perf log: ```
[12:09:58] alloc_workspace: requested=524288000, reserved=536870912
[12:09:58] kv_cache_use: before=1.1GB after=1.6GB (+500MB)
[12:10:01] cudamalloc failed: out of memory
```

nina_ops: Immediate mitigations we can flip from control plane now: 1) flip runtime flag to disable fused-gemm-v2 and fall back to fused-gemm-v1, 2) reduce per-shard workspace from 512MB -> 256MB, 3) lower max concurrency/batch size (concurrency 8 -> 4, max_batch_tokens 2048 -> 1024), 4) aggressive KV eviction TTL 60s -> 15s for inference-1, 5) enable model-variant fallback to quantized-xxsmall for requests > 1024 tokens. That should cut peak use significantly.

jeremy_k: Agreed. Quick API calls to toggle (use rollout-svc): ```bash
# disable new kernel
curl -X POST https://rollout.internal/api/flags -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"flag":"runtime.kernel.fused_gemm_v2","value":false,"target":"inference-1"}'

# shrink workspace
curl -X POST https://rollout.internal/api/flags -d '{"flag":"runtime.workspace.per_shard_mb","value":256,"target":"inference-1"}'

# lower batch concurrency
curl -X POST https://rollout.internal/api/flags -d '{"flag":"runtime.batch.max_concurrency","value":4,"target":"inference-1"}'
```

alex_chen: If we flip kernel off can we expect any correctness diffs? Also latency impact?

jeremy_k: fused-gemm-v1 is the previous validated kernel path — functional parity should be identical for current model shards. Latency for a single request might increase ~5-10% for some shapes but overall much better than falling over.

maria_gomez: I'll run a quick canary once flags are set. Plan: roll flags to 10% hosts in inference-1, observe OOM graph for 5 minutes, then 50% then 100%.

deploy-bot: flag-change: runtime.kernel.fused_gemm_v2 -> false (rolled to 10% hosts) by jeremy_k at 12:18 UTC

sam_patel: After 3m of canary: OOM rate dropped from 8/min -> 1/min on canary hosts. KV pressure reduced ~300MB on canary. Rolling to 50%.

deploy-bot: flag-change: runtime.workspace.per_shard_mb -> 256 rolled to 50% at 12:24 UTC

nina_ops: Also increased eviction aggressiveness — TTL->15s. That gave immediate headroom for bursts; keep it for the next 6hrs while we investigate root cause.

alex_chen: Great. Please add a short postmortem + checklist item to the incident tracker. We should document this exact mitigation sequence and add a guard in the kernel rollout job to validate peak workspace growth on a synthetic load before enabling.

maria_gomez: Adding follow-up tasks: 1) root cause perf regression analysis between fused-gemm-v1/v2 (profile diff), 2) add synthetic long-context soak in canary job, 3) permanent KV reuse patch (sam POC), 4) alert tuning (cudamalloc transient tolerance).

sam_patel: I'll open PR for buffer reuse and workspace-adaptive sizing — early numbers look promising (est. 30% less transient allocs).

jeremy_k: Note for on-call runbook: if you see cudamalloc OOM spikes after kernel rollouts do these steps in order: (A) narrow rollout -> disable kernel -> (B) shrink per_shard workspace -> (C) lower batch concurrency -> (D) evict KV aggressively / fallback to smaller model variant -> (E) if still failing, route to dedicated emergency pool. I'll add this to the runbook. :white_check_mark: 

alex_chen: Thanks team — monitoring shows OOMs near zero on inference-1 after full rollback and workspace shrink. We'll keep the temporary TTL and concurrency caps for 6 hours and track SLA impact. Follow-up sync in 2pm postmortem. :thumbsup:
